Read only that reference file for rcosteira (ignore the rest of compose here). If ahmed is effectively the sole source, say so — that is a valid "keep, unique to ahmed" outcome.

Produce:
1. contradictions — cases where two sources give ACTUALLY OPPOSING advice on the SAME specific technical point (not merely different depth or wording of the same principle). Name both sources (labels: "ahmed" / "chris" / "rcosteira"), state each claim, and cite evidence (file path + the specific lines/quote).
2. bugs — code that is broken, will not compile, or is technically WRONG (e.g. catches and swallows CancellationException, loses state across config change, references undefined symbols, wrong plugin/order). severity: critical | major | minor. Cite the file + evidence.
3. depthComparison — which source is most detailed/actionable here and why.
4. uniqueValue — what each source covers that the OTHERS DO NOT (worth keeping regardless of who dominates).

Be precise; cite real file content. Do NOT invent contradictions where sources only differ in depth — that is the most common false positive. Set cluster="navigation".

3	description: Jetpack Compose Navigation patterns - type-safe routes, NavHost setup, argument passing, deep links, nested navigation graphs, and bottom navigation.

5	
6	# Jetpack Compose Navigation Patterns
7	
8	## Dependencies
9	
10	```kotlin
11	dependencies {
12	    implementation("androidx.navigation:navigation-compose:2.8.5")
13	    implementation("org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-serialization-json:1.7.3")
14	}
15	```
16	
17	## Type-Safe Routes with Sealed Interface
18	
19	```kotlin
20	@Serializable
21	sealed interface Route {
22	    @Serializable
23	    data object Home : Route
24	
25	    @Serializable
26	    data object Settings : Route
27	
28	    @Serializable
29	    data class UserProfile(val userId: String) : Route
30	
31	    @Serializable
32	    data class PostDetail(val postId: Long, val showComments: Boolean = false) : Route
33	}
34	
35	// For nested graphs
36	@Serializable
37	sealed interface AuthGraph {
38	    @Serializable
39	    data object Login : AuthGraph
40	
41	    @Serializable
42	    data object Register : AuthGraph
43	
44	    @Serializable
45	    data object ForgotPassword : AuthGraph
46	}
47	```
48	
49	## NavHost Configuration
50	
51	```kotlin
52	@Composable
53	fun AppNavHost(
54	    navController: NavHostController = rememberNavController(),
55	    modifier: Modifier = Modifier
56	) {
57	    NavHost(
58	        navController = navController,
59	        startDestination = Route.Home,
60	        modifier = modifier
61	    ) {
62	        composable<Route.Home> {
63	            HomeScreen(
64	                onNavigateToProfile = { userId ->
65	                    navController.navigate(Route.UserProfile(userId))
66	                },
67	                onNavigateToSettings = {
68	                    navController.navigate(Route.Settings)
69	                }
70	            )
71	        }
72	
73	        composable<Route.Settings> {
74	            SettingsScreen(onBack = { navController.popBackStack() })
75	        }
76	
77	        composable<Route.UserProfile> { backStackEntry ->
78	            val route = backStackEntry.toRoute<Route.UserProfile>()
79	            UserProfileScreen(userId = route.userId)
80	        }
81	
82	        composable<Route.PostDetail> { backStackEntry ->
83	            val route = backStackEntry.toRoute<Route.PostDetail>()
84	            PostDetailScreen(
85	                postId = route.postId,
86	                showComments = route.showComments
87	            )
88	        }
89	    }
90	}
91	```
92	
93	## Argument Passing with Legacy navArgument
94	
95	For non-serializable routes, use the classic approach:
96	
97	```kotlin
98	composable(
99	    route = "post/{postId}?showComments={showComments}",
100	    arguments = listOf(
101	        navArgument("postId") { type = NavType.LongType },
102	        navArgument("showComments") {
103	            type = NavType.BoolType
104	            defaultValue = false
105	        }
106	    )
107	) { backStackEntry ->
108	    val postId = backStackEntry.arguments?.getLong("postId") ?: return@composable
109	    val showComments = backStackEntry.arguments?.getBoolean("showComments") ?: false
110	    PostDetailScreen(postId = postId, showComments = showComments)
111	}
112	
113	// Navigate
114	navController.navigate("post/$postId?showComments=true")
115	```
116	
117	## Navigation with Results (SavedStateHandle)
118	
119	```kotlin
120	// Screen A: Navigate and listen for result
121	@Composable
122	fun ScreenA(navController: NavHostController) {
123	    val result = navController.currentBackStackEntry
124	        ?.savedStateHandle
125	        ?.getStateFlow<String?>("selected_item", null)
126	        ?.collectAsState()
127	
128	    LaunchedEffect(result?.value) {
129	        result?.value?.let { item ->
130	            // Handle the result
131	        }
132	    }
133	
134	    Button(onClick = { navController.navigate(Route.ItemPicker) }) {
135	        Text("Pick Item")
136	    }
137	}
138	
139	// Screen B: Set result and go back
140	@Composable
141	fun ItemPickerScreen(navController: NavHostController) {
142	    Button(onClick = {
143	        navController.previousBackStackEntry
144	            ?.savedStateHandle
145	            ?.set("selected_item", "chosen_value")
146	        navController.popBackStack()
147	    }) {
148	        Text("Select This")
149	    }
150	}
151	```
152	
153	## Deep Link Registration
154	
155	```kotlin
156	composable<Route.PostDetail>(
157	    deepLinks = listOf(
158	        navDeepLink {
159	            uriPattern = "https://example.com/posts/{postId}"
160	        },
161	        navDeepLink {
162	            uriPattern = "myapp://posts/{postId}"
163	        }
164	    )
165	) { backStackEntry ->
166	    val route = backStackEntry.toRoute<Route.PostDetail>()
167	    PostDetailScreen(postId = route.postId)
168	}
169	```
170	
171	AndroidManifest.xml intent filter:
172	
173	```xml
174	<activity android:name=".MainActivity">
175	    <intent-filter>
176	        <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
177	        <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
178	        <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
179	        <data android:scheme="https" android:host="example.com" />
180	        <data android:scheme="myapp" />
181	    </intent-filter>
182	</activity>
183	```
184	
185	## Nested Navigation Graphs
186	
187	```kotlin
188	fun NavGraphBuilder.authNavGraph(navController: NavHostController) {
189	    navigation<AuthGraph.Login>(startDestination = AuthGraph.Login) {
190	        composable<AuthGraph.Login> {
191	            LoginScreen(
192	                onLoginSuccess = {
193	                    navController.navigate(Route.Home) {
194	                        popUpTo(AuthGraph.Login) { inclusive = true }
195	                    }
196	                },
197	                onNavigateToRegister = {
198	                    navController.navigate(AuthGraph.Register)
199	                }
200	            )
201	        }
202	        composable<AuthGraph.Register> {
203	            RegisterScreen(onBack = { navController.popBackStack() })
204	        }
205	        composable<AuthGraph.ForgotPassword> {
206	            ForgotPasswordScreen(onBack = { navController.popBackStack() })
207	        }
208	    }
209	}
210	
211	// In the main NavHost
212	NavHost(navController = navController, startDestination = AuthGraph.Login) {
213	    authNavGraph(navController)
214	    composable<Route.Home> { HomeScreen() }
215	}
216	```
217	
218	## Bottom Navigation
219	
220	```kotlin
221	@Serializable
222	sealed interface BottomTab {
223	    @Serializable data object Feed : BottomTab
224	    @Serializable data object Search : BottomTab
225	    @Serializable data object Profile : BottomTab
226	}
227	
228	data class BottomNavItem(
229	    val route: BottomTab,
230	    val label: String,
231	    val icon: ImageVector
232	)
233	
234	val bottomNavItems = listOf(
235	    BottomNavItem(BottomTab.Feed, "Feed", Icons.Default.Home),
236	    BottomNavItem(BottomTab.Search, "Search", Icons.Default.Search),
237	    BottomNavItem(BottomTab.Profile, "Profile", Icons.Default.Person)
238	)
239	
240	@Composable
241	fun MainScreen() {
242	    val navController = rememberNavController()
243	    val navBackStackEntry by navController.currentBackStackEntryAsState()
244	
245	    Scaffold(
246	        bottomBar = {
247	            NavigationBar {
248	                bottomNavItems.forEach { item ->
249	                    val isSelected = navBackStackEntry?.destination?.hasRoute(
250	                        item.route::class
251	                    ) == true
252	
253	                    NavigationBarItem(
254	                        selected = isSelected,
255	                        onClick = {
256	                            navController.navigate(item.route) {
257	                                popUpTo(navController.graph.findStartDestination().id) {
258	                                    saveState = true
259	                                }
260	                                launchSingleTop = true
261	                                restoreState = true
262	                            }
263	                        },
264	                        icon = { Icon(item.icon, contentDescription = item.label) },
265	                        label = { Text(item.label) }
266	                    )
267	                }
268	            }
269	        }
270	    ) { padding ->
271	        NavHost(
272	            navController = navController,
273	            startDestination = BottomTab.Feed,
274	            modifier = Modifier.padding(padding)
275	        ) {
276	            composable<BottomTab.Feed> { FeedScreen() }
277	            composable<BottomTab.Search> { SearchScreen() }
278	            composable<BottomTab.Profile> { ProfileScreen() }
279	        }
280	    }
281	}
282	```
283	
284	## Animated Transitions
285	
286	```kotlin
287	composable<Route.PostDetail>(
288	    enterTransition = {
289	        slideIntoContainer(
290	            towards = AnimatedContentTransitionScope.SlideDirection.Left,
291	            animationSpec = tween(300)
292	        )
293	    },
294	    exitTransition = {
295	        slideOutOfContainer(
296	            towards = AnimatedContentTransitionScope.SlideDirection.Left,
297	            animationSpec = tween(300)
298	        )
299	    },
300	    popEnterTransition = {
301	        slideIntoContainer(
302	            towards = AnimatedContentTransitionScope.SlideDirection.Right,
303	            animationSpec = tween(300)
304	        )
305	    },
306	    popExitTransition = {
307	        slideOutOfContainer(
308	            towards = AnimatedContentTransitionScope.SlideDirection.Right,
309	            animationSpec = tween(300)
310	        )
311	    }
312	) { backStackEntry ->
313	    val route = backStackEntry.toRoute<Route.PostDetail>()
314	    PostDetailScreen(postId = route.postId)
315	}
316	```
317	
318	## Navigation Testing
319	
320	```kotlin
321	@Test
322	fun navigateToProfile_displaysUserProfile() {
323	    val navController = TestNavHostController(ApplicationProvider.getApplicationContext())
324	
325	    composeTestRule.setContent {
326	        navController.navigatorProvider.addNavigator(ComposeNavigator())
327	        AppNavHost(navController = navController)
328	    }
329	
330	    composeTestRule.onNodeWithText("View Profile").performClick()
331	
332	    val currentRoute = navController.currentBackStackEntry?.destination?.route
333	    assertTrue(currentRoute?.contains("UserProfile") == true)
334	}
335	```
336	
337	## Best Practices
338	
339	- Use type-safe routes with `@Serializable` data classes/objects over raw string routes.
340	- Keep navigation logic out of composables; pass lambda callbacks (`onNavigateTo`) instead.
341	- Use `popUpTo` with `inclusive = true` when navigating after login to clear the auth stack.
342	- Use `launchSingleTop = true` for bottom tabs to prevent duplicate destinations.
343	- Save and restore tab state with `saveState = true` and `restoreState = true`.
344	- Scope ViewModels to navigation entries with `hiltViewModel()` or `koinViewModel()`.
345	- Test navigation by asserting on `navController.currentBackStackEntry`.
346

25	data object HomeScreen : Screen
26

28	data class DetailScreen(val id: String) : Screen

32	    Navigator(HomeScreen) { navigator ->

252	## State Preservation
253	
254	### Voyager ScreenModel
255	
256	```kotlin
257	class DetailScreenModel(
258	    private val userId: String,
259	    private val repository: UserRepository
260	) : ScreenModel {
261	    val user = mutableStateOf<User?>(null)
262	    val isLoading = mutableStateOf(false)
263	
264	    init {
265	        loadUser()
266	    }
267	
268	    private fun loadUser() {
269	        viewModelScope.launch {
270	            isLoading.value = true
271	            user.value = repository.getUser(userId)
272	            isLoading.value = false
273	        }
274	    }
275	}
276	
277	@Composable
278	fun DetailScreen(
279	    userId: String,
280	    onBack: () -> Unit
281	) {
282	    val model = rememberScreenModel { DetailScreenModel(userId) }
283	
284	    if (model.isLoading.value) {
285	        CircularProgressIndicator()
286	    } else {
287	        model.user.value?.let { user ->
288	            UserContent(user, onBack)
289	        }
290	    }
291	}
292	```
293

295	
296	**Remember**: Choose navigation library based on project needs. Voyager for simplicity, Decompose for control, platform-native for full platform feature support.

5	
6	# Deep Linking Patterns for Mobile
7	
8	## URI Scheme Design
9	
10	Design a consistent URI scheme before implementation:
11	
12	```
13	myapp://                          # App root
14	myapp://home                      # Home screen
15	myapp://product/{id}              # Product detail
16	myapp://profile/{userId}          # User profile
17	myapp://settings/notifications    # Nested settings
18	myapp://search?q={query}          # Query parameters
19	```
20	
21	Keep paths RESTful, lowercase, and predictable. Use path segments for hierarchy and query params for filters.
22	
23	---
24	
25	## Android
26	
27	### Intent Filter in AndroidManifest.xml
28	
29	```xml
30	<activity
31	    android:name=".MainActivity"
32	    android:exported="true">
33	
34	    <!-- Custom URI scheme -->
35	    <intent-filter>
36	        <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
37	        <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
38	        <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
39	        <data
40	            android:scheme="myapp"
41	            android:host="product"
42	            android:pathPrefix="/" />
43	    </intent-filter>
44	
45	    <!-- App Links (HTTPS verified) -->
46	    <intent-filter android:autoVerify="true">
47	        <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
48	        <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
49	        <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
50	        <data
51	            android:scheme="https"
52	            android:host="www.myapp.com"
53	            android:pathPrefix="/product" />
54	    </intent-filter>
55	</activity>
56	```
57	
58	### App Links with assetlinks.json
59	
60	Host at `https://www.myapp.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json`:
61	
62	```json
63	[{
64	  "relation": ["delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls"],
65	  "target": {
66	    "namespace": "android_app",
67	    "package_name": "com.myapp.android",
68	    "sha256_cert_fingerprints": [
69	      "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99:AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99"
70	    ]
71	  }
72	}]
73	```
74	
75	Get your certificate fingerprint:
76	```bash
77	keytool -list -v -keystore my-release-key.keystore -alias my-key-alias
78	```
79	
80	### Handling Deep Links in Activity
81	
82	```kotlin
83	class MainActivity : ComponentActivity() {
84	    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
85	        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
86	        handleDeepLink(intent)
87	    }
88	
89	    override fun onNewIntent(intent: Intent) {
90	        super.onNewIntent(intent)
91	        handleDeepLink(intent)
92	    }
93	
94	    private fun handleDeepLink(intent: Intent) {
95	        val uri = intent.data ?: return
96	        val path = uri.path ?: return
97	        val segments = path.split("/").filter { it.isNotEmpty() }
98	
99	        when {
100	            segments.firstOrNull() == "product" -> {
101	                val productId = segments.getOrNull(1)
102	                navigateToProduct(productId)

contradictions.claimA: Navigation 3 is the default for new work; Navigation 2 (NavHost/NavController) is explicitly legacy/interop. 'Default to Navigation 3 for new work — Nav3 all the way unless impossible ... the Navigation 2 patterns above are legacy/interop.'
contradictions.claimB: Builds its entire recommended Compose-navigation approach on Navigation 2 (navigation-compose 2.8.5, NavHost + NavController + composable<Route>) and presents it as current best practice, with zero mention of Navigation 3.
contradictions.evidence: rcosteira compose/references/navigation.md lines 3 ('Navigation 3 (androidx.navigation3) is the default for new work'), 16-18 ('Default to Navigation 3 for new work — Nav3 all the way unless impossible', 'the Navigation 2 patterns above are legacy/interop'). ahmed navigation-compose/SKILL.md lines 10-14 (implementation('androidx.navigation:navigation-compose:2.8.5')), 51-91 (NavHost/NavController as THE setup), 337-345 Best Practices — no Nav3 reference anywhere. When both skills auto-trigger on Compose nav code the agent gets opposing direction: use NavHost/NavController (ahmed) vs NavHost/NavController is legacy, use Nav3 (rcosteira).

contradictions.topic: String routes vs type-safe @Serializable routes, and mixing the two in one project
contradictions.claimA: 'Type-safe @Serializable route classes, never string routes' and lists 'don't mix string and type-safe routes' as an explicit trap to avoid.
contradictions.claimB: Endorses string routes as a valid classic approach ('For non-serializable routes, use the classic approach') and actively uses string routes alongside type-safe ones across its skills, i.e. exactly the mixing rcosteira forbids.
contradictions.evidence: rcosteira compose/references/navigation.md line 9 ('never string routes'), line 12 (trap: 'don't mix string and type-safe routes'). ahmed navigation-compose/SKILL.md lines 93-115 ('Argument Passing with Legacy navArgument', route = "post/{postId}?showComments={showComments}") presented next to type-safe routes; ahmed deep-linking/SKILL.md lines 116-128 (route = "product/{productId}" with navArgument); ahmed kmp-navigation/SKILL.md lines 122-132 (composable("detail/{id}")).

bugs.description: The Activity deep-link handler cannot route the custom URI scheme it declares. The manifest registers the custom scheme with 'product' as the HOST (android:scheme="myapp" android:host="product"), so myapp://product/123 has host=product and path=/123. But handleDeepLink() reads uri.path, splits it, and matches segments.firstOrNull() == "product". For myapp://product/123 the path is only "/123", so segments=["123"] and the 'product' branch never matches — the custom-scheme deep link silently does nothing. (It happens to work for the https App Link www.myapp.com/product/123 where 'product' really is a path segment.) The documented test command adb ... -d "myapp://product/123" would therefore fail to route.
bugs.evidence: Manifest lines 39-43 (scheme=myapp, host=product, pathPrefix=/). Handler lines 94-108: 'val uri = intent.data ...; val path = uri.path ...; segments = path.split("/")...; segments.firstOrNull() == "product"'. Test line 254: adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "myapp://product/123".

bugs.description: Decompose example references an undefined symbol 'Decomanavigation(...)' as the navigation host. No such API exists in Decompose (the real API is Children(stack) / ChildStack with a StackNavigation). As written the recommended-alternative example will not compile.
bugs.evidence: Line 76: 'Decomanavigation(' followed by navigator=, initialConfiguration=. Decompose 2.x uses StackNavigation + childStack + Children(...).

bugs.description: Swift syntax embedded in a Kotlin function. In iosMain (Kotlin), 'fun toSwiftUI() -> some View { ... }' uses Swift's return-arrow and opaque-type ('-> some View') syntax; Kotlin uses ': ReturnType'. This will not compile as Kotlin.
bugs.evidence: Line 141: 'fun toSwiftUI() -> some View {' inside 'actual class Navigator' in the iosMain block (lines 137-144).

bugs.description: Name clash / redeclaration: an interface named 'Navigator' and a class named 'Navigator' are declared in the same scope, with 'expect class Navigator() : Navigator' and 'actual class Navigator : Navigator'. A classifier cannot share its name with the interface it implements in the same package — this is a redeclaration conflict and will not compile.
bugs.evidence: Line 105 'interface Navigator { ... }', line 111 'expect class Navigator() : Navigator', lines 114 and 137 'actual class Navigator : Navigator'.

bugs.description: Voyager ScreenModel uses the wrong coroutine scope. DetailScreenModel extends Voyager's ScreenModel but launches with 'viewModelScope.launch { ... }'. ScreenModel does not expose viewModelScope (that is AndroidX ViewModel); Voyager provides 'screenModelScope'. 'viewModelScope' is an unresolved reference here and will not compile.
bugs.evidence: Lines 257-275: 'class DetailScreenModel(...) : ScreenModel { ... init { loadUser() } private fun loadUser() { viewModelScope.launch { ... } } }'.

bugs.description: Missing required constructor argument. DetailScreenModel is declared with two required params (userId: String, repository: UserRepository) but is instantiated as 'rememberScreenModel { DetailScreenModel(userId) }' with only userId — the repository argument is omitted, so it will not compile.
bugs.evidence: Constructor lines 257-260 'class DetailScreenModel(private val userId: String, private val repository: UserRepository)'. Call site line 282 'val model = rememberScreenModel { DetailScreenModel(userId) }'.

bugs.description: The Voyager 'Recommended' example does not compile. (1) 'VoyagerNavigation(navigator = ..., screenModels = ...)' is an undefined symbol — no such Voyager API (the standard is CurrentScreen() inside Navigator{}). (2) 'data object HomeScreen : Screen' and 'data class DetailScreen(...) : Screen' implement Voyager's Screen interface but never override its abstract '@Composable fun Content()', so they are invalid Screen implementations.
bugs.evidence: Lines 24-38: '@Serializable data object HomeScreen : Screen', '@Serializable data class DetailScreen(val id: String) : Screen', 'Navigator(HomeScreen) { navigator -> VoyagerNavigation(navigator = navigator, screenModels = { rememberScreenModel { AppScreenModel() } }) }'. No Content() override on either Screen; VoyagerNavigation is not a Voyager symbol.

bugs.description: Android-only Parcelable/@Parcelize used in commonMain KMP code. Every route/config sealed class in this file lives in commonMain (per the file-path comments) yet extends 'Parcelable' with '@Parcelize' members. android.os.Parcelable and the kotlin-parcelize @Parcelize are Android-only and are not resolvable in commonMain. The file shows NO imports and no Essenty (com.arkivanov.essenty.parcelable) or expect/actual Parcelable setup, so as written this shared code will not compile for non-Android targets. Line 227-229 also redundantly combines '@Serializable sealed class Screen : Parcelable', mixing two serialization frameworks.
bugs.evidence: Lines 63-64 ('// commonMain/kotlin/navigation/DecomposeNavigation.kt' then 'sealed class Config : Parcelable {'), 95-97, 199-200, 227-229; @Parcelize at lines 65,68,98,101,201,204,230,233,239. No import statements anywhere in the file.

bugs.description: Nested-graph example uses the same route type for the graph and one of its child destinations. 'navigation<AuthGraph.Login>(startDestination = AuthGraph.Login) { composable<AuthGraph.Login> { ... } }' makes the NavGraph's own route (AuthGraph.Login) identical to a destination registered inside it. Nav Compose throws when a destination has the same route as its parent graph, so the graph fails to build at runtime (crash when the NavHost composes). The graph marker should be a distinct type (e.g. the AuthGraph interface), not AuthGraph.Login.

Recommends a shut-down service. The deferred-deep-link section tells users to use Firebase Dynamic Links (Firebase.dynamicLinks.getDynamicLink(intent)). Firebase Dynamic Links was deprecated and fully shut down on 25 Aug 2025; as of the current date this API/service no longer functions, so the guidance and snippet are technically wrong for new work (AppsFlyer/Branch or a custom deferred-link solution should be used instead).
bugs.evidence: Lines 131-142: 'Use Firebase Dynamic Links or AppsFlyer for deferred deep links that survive app install' followed by 'Firebase.dynamicLinks.getDynamicLink(intent).addOnSuccessListener { ... }'.

input.depthComparison:
Only two of the three named sources have navigation content in scope: ahmed (three dedicated skills) and rcosteira (a single references/navigation.md inside the compose skill). There is no 'chris' navigation content here, so this cluster is an ahmed-vs-rcosteira comparison.

For raw depth and actionability, AHMED dominates. It ships three code-heavy skills: navigation-compose (type-safe routes, NavHost, args, savedStateHandle result passing, deep links, nested graphs, bottom nav with saveState/restoreState/launchSingleTop, animated transitions, TestNavHostController testing, best practices), kmp-navigation (Voyager/Decompose/platform-native expect-actual bridge, tabs, KMP deep linking, type-safe args, state preservation), and deep-linking (Android App Links + assetlinks.json + keytool, iOS Universal Links + AASA + Associated Domains, Info.plist URL schemes, SceneDelegate/AppDelegate + SwiftUI onOpenURL, deferred links, adb/simctl test commands, analytics). Nobody else comes close on breadth or copy-pasteable volume. The caveat is quality: several ahmed snippets are buggy or won't compile (see bugs), and the kmp-navigation file in particular is riddled with non-compiling code.

For correctness and currency, RCOSTEIRA is stronger despite being a fraction of the length. It is the only source that (a) treats Navigation 3 as the default for new work and correctly labels Nav2 as legacy/interop, (b) deliberately delegates Nav3 detail to Google's official navigation-3 skill and the nav3-recipes repo to avoid drift, and (c) supplies high-signal architectural guardrails ahmed lacks entirely (serializable destination keys as fields not captured callbacks, no @Composable lambdas in destination data, ViewModels emitting Flow<NavEvent> collected in a LaunchedEffect rather than holding a NavController, and correct nav-entry decorator nesting order). It is thin on ready-to-paste code but architecturally more correct and forward-looking.

Net: keep ahmed for the concrete Nav2 recipes and the cross-platform deep-linking breadth (after fixing the bugs), and keep rcosteira for Nav3-first direction and the compose-shape guardrails. Where they disagree (Nav2-vs-Nav3 as default; string routes), rcosteira reflects current Android guidance.

uniqueValue.whatIsUnique: The only source covering the full deep-linking stack across BOTH platforms: Android intent-filters + App Links autoVerify + hosted assetlinks.json + keytool fingerprint extraction; iOS Universal Links + apple-app-site-association + Associated Domains; Info.plist CFBundleURLTypes; SceneDelegate/AppDelegate handling + SwiftUI .onOpenURL; a Swift DeepLinkRouter architecture; deferred/deferred-attribution deep links; adb and xcrun simctl openurl test commands; and deep-link analytics tracking. rcosteira only mentions navDeepLink in a single clause.

The only source addressing Kotlin Multiplatform navigation at all: Voyager, Decompose, and a platform-native expect/actual Navigator bridge (Compose Nav on Android, SwiftUI on iOS), plus cross-platform tab navigation, KMP type-safe arguments, and Voyager ScreenModel state preservation. (Topic coverage is unique even though much of the code has compile bugs.)

Full worked recipes that the others only name in passing: a complete bottom-navigation multi-back-stack setup (popUpTo(findStartDestination) with saveState/restoreState/launchSingleTop), per-destination animated transitions via enterTransition/exitTransition/popEnter/popExit, a navigate-for-result flow using previousBackStackEntry.savedStateHandle, and a runnable TestNavHostController navigation test.

The only source covering Navigation 3 (androidx.navigation3): NavDisplay + entryProvider with the back stack owned as observable state and no NavController/graph builder; pointers to Google's installable navigation-3 skill and the nav3-recipes repo instead of duplicating it; and the 'compose-shape guardrails' (destination keys as top-level @Serializable fields not captured callbacks; no @Composable lambdas in destination data; ViewModels emit Flow<NavEvent>/Channel(BUFFERED).receiveAsFlow() collected in a LaunchedEffect rather than holding a NavController; rememberSaveableStateHolderNavEntryDecorator must wrap rememberViewModelStoreNavEntryDecorator; don't wrap NavDisplay content in AnimatedContent). Ahmed covers none of Nav3 or these guardrails.
